heading: All-pairs shortest paths in one pass
body:
**Floyd-Warshall** computes shortest paths between **every pair of cities** in O(V³).

The core trick: for each intermediate vertex **k**, check if routing through **k** beats the direct route:

`dist[i][j] = min(dist[i][j], dist[i][k] + dist[k][j])`

**When to use**: V ≤ 100 makes O(V³) practical.

heading: Loop order is critical
body:
**The k-loop MUST be outermost:**

```
for k in range(n):  # intermediate
  for i in range(n):  # source
    for j in range(n):  # destination
```

Why? When considering paths through vertex **k**, you need the best paths using vertices 0..k-1 already computed.

label: Crux · Python

q: What is the time complexity of Floyd-Warshall?
explain: Three nested loops over all vertices (k, i, j) → O(V³).
